source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.6 Work, Energy and Power, §6.2 Notions of work and kinetic energy: the work-energy theorem — table-of-contents scope only, teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: the NET work done on a body equals the change in its kinetic energy, W_net = ΔK = ½mv² − ½mv₀², and only that. Does NOT cover what work is or W = F·d·cos θ (work_done_by_constant_force); the sign taxonomy of work or net work as a signed sum (positive_negative_zero_work — assumed, not re-taught); what kinetic energy is (kinetic_energy_definition); whether a force's work depends on the path (conservative_vs_nonconservative_forces); potential energy of any kind; or where removed kinetic energy goes — heat, sound, the micro story (mechanical_energy_loss_with_friction) — or power. Boundary with kinetic_energy_definition enforced mechanically: this is the first concept in the fleet to author work bars and the K bar TOGETHER in one panel — every state authors both a non-empty energy_layer.bars (exactly [K]) and at least one work_accumulators entry, which is what makes the engine's own panel header read 'Energy and work bars' — kinetic_energy_definition said 'Energy bars', work_done_by_constant_force and positive_negative_zero_work said 'Work done'. Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine with the SEAM K/L/M/N energy layer (docs/loop_runs/ch6_state.md). Pure configuration, zero renderer edits (0d).

real_world_anchor.primary: Braking a moving vehicle. To stop, the brakes and the road must do negative net work exactly equal to the vehicle's kinetic energy — every joule of half m v squared must be matched by a joule of negative net work before the speed reaches zero. Twice the speed means four times the kinetic energy, so four times the net work to remove.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Catching a ball. Your hands must do negative net work equal to the ball's kinetic energy. Moving your hands backward while catching spreads the same joules over a longer distance, so the force on your hands is smaller — same work, longer distance, smaller force.

v0.name: launch speed at the state's own start (signed)

mu_k.name: coefficient of kinetic friction (S2, S3, S6 only)

mu_s.name: coefficient of static friction (authored equal to mu_k, S2/S3/S6 only)

d.name: displacement from the state's own initial_position_m

formulas.the_theorem: W_net = delta K = half m v^2 minus half m v0^2 -- the ONE idea this concept teaches (every state)
formulas.derivation_chain: W_net = m a d, and v^2 = v0^2 + 2 a d, therefore W_net = half m v^2 minus half m v0^2 -- S5's derivation, checked by the stamp
formulas.pull_work_constant_force: W_pull = F d -- valid whenever F is a constant force, even through a velocity reversal (S4 -- constant-force work is path-independent, it depends only on net displacement)
formulas.friction_work: W_friction = -mu_k * m * g * d -- valid because the cart never reverses direction while friction acts anywhere in this concept (S2, S3, S6), so d equals the distance actually slid
formulas.s3_exact_balance: F = mu_k * m * g = 19.6 N exactly, so a = 0 identically, so W_net = 0 identically (S3)

constraints: W_net = delta K = half m v^2 minus half m v0^2 at every instant, in every state of this concept -- this is the theorem itself, not a special case
when exactly one force acts on the body, that force's own work equals the net work exactly (S1, S2, S4, S5 -- each authors ONLY a net accumulator for this reason)
for a CONSTANT force, W = F times the net displacement, regardless of any velocity reversal in between (S4 -- work is path-independent for a constant force)
kinetic friction's work is never positive while the body slides, and holds at its last value once the body is at rest (S2, S3, S6)
kinetic energy K = half m v^2 is never negative; the net-work bar CAN be negative -- K and W_net are different kinds of quantity read on different instruments
g = 9.8 m/s^2 (constant, NLB_G); every surface in this concept is flat, so no angle enters any formula and gravity does identically zero work throughout

aha_moment.statement: The work meter and the energy meter are the same meter, reading the same number.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: A crate pulled from rest by a steady 10 N force: the net-work bar and the K bar always read the same number, frame by frame, reaching exactly 40.0 J by the loop end.

STATE_1.title: Net work equals the kinetic energy gained

scene_composition.text: a ten newton pull acts on this crate, the only horizontal force, from rest on a frictionless floor
the combined panel at the left edge shows the net-work bar and the K bar climbing together, both landing on exactly 40.0 J
the HUD's v row climbs from 0.00 to 4.00 m/s, and the formula surface reads Wₙₑₜ = ΔK

tts_sentences.text_en: A ten newton pull acts on this crate, the only force, so its work is the whole net work.
tts_sentences.text_hi: इस crate पर दस newton का एक pull लगता है, यह अकेला force है, इसलिए इसका work पूरा net work है।

tts_sentences.text_en: The work bar climbs as the pull acts over distance, force times metres.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Work bar उतना ही चढ़ता है जितनी दूरी तक pull काम करता है, force गुणा metres।

tts_sentences.text_en: The K bar reads the crate kinetic energy, the energy a moving body has.
tts_sentences.text_hi: K bar crate की kinetic energy दिखाता है, वह energy जो एक चलती हुई body के पास होती है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Both bars always match, reaching forty joules each cycle.
tts_sentences.text_hi: दोनों bars हमेशा बराबर रहते हैं, हर cycle में चालीस joules तक पहुँचते हैं।

STATE_2.title: Negative net work removes kinetic energy

scene_composition.text: the crate is already moving at four metres per second onto a rough floor, with no pull — only friction acts
the net bar dives below the zero line to −40.0 J as the K bar falls from 40.0 J to exactly 0.0 J
the friction arrow vanishes once the crate stops, and the HUD's v row holds at 0.00 m/s

tts_sentences.text_en: The crate is already moving at four metres per second, and only friction acts.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Crate पहले से ही चार metres per second की speed से चल रही है, और सिर्फ friction काम कर रही है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Friction points against the motion, so its work counts negative.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction motion के खिलाफ point करती है, इसलिए इसका work negative गिना जाता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: The net bar dives below zero as the K bar falls toward zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Net bar zero से नीचे गिरता है जैसे K bar भी zero की तरफ गिरता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: The crate stops: net holds at minus forty joules, K at zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Crate रुक जाती है: net minus चालीस joules पर रुकता है, K zero पर।

STATE_3.title: Only the net work changes kinetic energy

scene_composition.text: the pull and kinetic friction are authored exactly equal, 19.6 N each, so the crate coasts at a constant 2.5 m/s
three work bars run at once: the pull bar climbs to +98.0 J, the friction bar dives to −98.0 J, and the net bar sits parked on the zero line
the K bar holds flat at 15.6 J the whole loop while the d arrow grows, and the HUD's F and f rows both read 19.6 N

tts_sentences.text_en: The pull and friction are equal, nineteen point six newtons, and the crate coasts.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Pull और friction बराबर हैं, उन्नीस point six newtons, और crate coast करती है।

tts_sentences.text_en: The pull bar climbs steadily, reaching ninety-eight joules by the loop's end.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Pull का bar अट्ठानवे joules तक, हर loop के अंत में, लगातार चढ़ता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Friction bar dives just as far, so the two always cancel to zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Friction का bar भी उतना ही गिरता है, तो दोनों हमेशा cancel होकर zero बनाते हैं।

tts_sentences.text_en: Only the net counts: the K bar holds flat at fifteen point six joules.
tts_sentences.text_hi: सिर्फ net गिनती में आता है: K bar पंद्रह point six joules पर flat रहता है।

misconception_watch.belief: The work done by the force you apply becomes kinetic energy
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The pull bar climbs to +98.0 J — the number the belief tracks — while the K bar holds 15.6 J without moving and the net bar sits on its zero line
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Only the net work changes kinetic energy — add the works with their signs first.

STATE_4.title: Change measured from the starting energy

scene_composition.text: a 4 kg cart launches backward at three metres a second against a steady twelve newton pull, on a frictionless floor
the net bar dives to −18.0 J exactly as the K bar falls to 0.0 J at the turn, then both climb back — K to 46.1 J beside net at +28.1 J
the HUD's v row crosses zero at the turn, and the formula surface reads ΔK = ½mv² − ½mv₀²

tts_sentences.text_en: This cart starts backward at three metres a second, pulled by twelve newtons.
tts_sentences.text_hi: यह cart पीछे की ओर तीन metres per second से शुरू होती है, बारह newtons से खींची जाती है।

tts_sentences.text_en: At the turn, net dives to minus eighteen joules as K reads zero.
tts_sentences.text_hi: जैसे यह धीमी होती है, मोड़ पर net minus अट्ठारह joules तक गिरता है जब K zero दिखाता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: By the end, K climbs to forty-six point one, net to plus twenty-eight point one.
tts_sentences.text_hi: अंत तक, K छियालीस point one तक पहुँचता है, net plus अट्ठाइस point one तक।

tts_sentences.text_en: Two nonzero numbers: net measures the change from the start, not the final energy.
tts_sentences.text_hi: दो non-zero numbers: net शुरुआत से बदलाव मापता है, आखिरी energy को नहीं।

misconception_watch.belief: Net work equals the final half m v squared
misconception_watch.visual_counter: At the end of the run the K bar reads 46.1 J while the net bar reads +28.1 J — two different nonzero numbers on one screen; the change is 46.1 minus 18.0 equals 28.1, measured from the starting 18.0 J
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: W_net equals half m v squared minus half m v0 squared, the change, not the final value.

STATE_5.title: The theorem comes from F = ma

scene_composition.text: a five newton pull speeds up this cart from two metres a second on a frictionless floor
at the flag the stamp reads flag: W net = 10.0 J · K = 20.0 J, appended beneath the formula surface
the d arrow shows exactly 2.0 m at the flag, and the HUD's a row holds at 1.00 m/s²

tts_sentences.text_en: A five newton pull speeds up this cart from two metres a second.
tts_sentences.text_hi: पाँच newton का pull इस cart को दो metres per second से तेज़ करता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Net work, mass times acceleration times distance, equals the change in kinetic energy.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Net work — mass गुणा acceleration गुणा distance — kinetic energy में बदलाव के बराबर होता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: At the flag, the pull has done ten joules while K rises from ten to twenty.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Flag पर, pull ने दस joules का work किया है जबकि K दस से बीस joules तक बढ़ता है।

tts_sentences.text_en: Ten and ten agree: five newtons times two metres matches the d arrow.
tts_sentences.text_hi: दस और दस मिलते हैं: पाँच newtons गुणा दो metres भी d arrow की reading से मिलता है।

STATE_6.title: Explore: force, mass and starting speed

scene_composition.text: three live sliders — force, mass and starting speed — drive the cart on a rough floor
the pull, friction and net work bars and the K meter re-derive every frame as the sliders move
dragging the crate repositions it and stops it — the honest way to park it and read K fresh

tts_sentences.text_en: Change the force, the mass, and the starting speed.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Force, mass, और starting speed बदलिए।

tts_sentences.text_en: Watch the work bars and the K bar together.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Work bars और K bar को साथ देखिए।

tts_sentences.text_en: The net bar always matches the change in K.
tts_sentences.text_hi: Net bar हमेशा K में बदलाव से मिलता है।

regeneration_variants.label: A Delivery Cart Rolling Across a Warehouse Floor
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A delivery cart is pulled from rest across a level warehouse floor. A second cart launched at speed slides to a stop under the floor's own friction, and a third is pulled at exactly the speed friction would otherwise remove.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical readings: the same net-work bar and K meter, the same lockstep climb from a steady pull, the same fall to exactly zero under friction alone, and the same net-zero hold when a pull exactly balances friction.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-body rig, same flat floor — only the labelled object changes from a cart to a delivery cart.

regeneration_variants.label: A Hockey Puck Launched Across a Rink
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A hockey puck is struck and slides across the ice under a steady push; a second puck launched with no push slides to a stop under the ice's own friction; a third turns around against a steady push and speeds back up.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same theorem, same numbers: the puck's net-work bar and its K meter always read the same joules, signed the same way, through every turn.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same rig and physics — the cart is relabelled a puck, the floor becomes the rink.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who has mastered this concept can state the work-energy theorem W_net = delta K = half m v squared minus half m v0 squared; compute the net work or the change in kinetic energy given the other; explain why the work done by one force is not automatically the net work when other forces also act; explain why a nonzero individual force's work can leave kinetic energy unchanged when it sums to zero with another force's work; correctly measure the change in kinetic energy from the STARTING value rather than treating net work as the final kinetic energy alone, including through a velocity reversal; and derive the theorem from F = ma and v squared = v-naught squared plus 2ad.

questions.stem: A 5 kg crate starts from rest and a steady 10 N pull acts on it as the ONLY force, on a frictionless floor. After the crate has moved 4 m, what is the net work done on it, and what is its kinetic energy at that instant?

distractor_misconceptions.B: halves F times d for no physical reason — an arithmetic slip, not a conceptual one, but a common one
distractor_misconceptions.C: computes K by dropping the one-half factor (uses m v squared instead of half m v squared)
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses the force's own magnitude (10 N) with the work it does, ignoring the distance moved entirely

questions.tested_idea: the theorem itself, positive case: W_net = F*d and K = half m v^2 agree exactly
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 4 kg block starts from rest and a steady 8 N force pushes it across a frictionless floor for 5 m. Find the net work done and the block's kinetic energy at that point.

questions.stem: A 5 kg crate slides at 4 m/s onto a rough floor (mu = 0.4) with no applied force, and friction alone brings it to rest. What is the net work done by friction while the crate slides to a stop, and what is the crate's kinetic energy at the moment it stops?

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the sign, forgetting that a force opposing the motion does negative work even though it is a real, positive-magnitude force
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses the ORIGINAL kinetic energy with the CURRENT one, as if a body that once had speed keeps that energy after stopping
distractor_misconceptions.D: believes work requires an applied push — misses that friction is itself a force doing (negative) work on the sliding body

questions.tested_idea: the theorem is signed: a force opposing the motion does negative net work, and K falls to exactly zero at rest
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 2 kg puck slides at 6 m/s onto a rough patch (mu = 0.3) with no applied force and slides to a stop. Find the net work done by friction and the puck's final kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A 5 kg crate coasts at a constant 2.5 m/s while a 19.6 N pull exactly balances 19.6 N of kinetic friction. After the crate has travelled 5 m, what is the NET work done on it, and how has its kinetic energy changed?

options.A: Net work = 0 J; kinetic energy is unchanged
options.B: Net work = 98.0 J (the pull's own work); kinetic energy increased by 98.0 J
options.C: Net work = −98.0 J (friction's own work); kinetic energy decreased by 98.0 J
options.D: Net work = 196.0 J (both forces added as sizes); kinetic energy increased sharply

distractor_misconceptions.B: the concept's headline misconception: mistakes ONE force's own work (the pull's) for the NET work on the body
distractor_misconceptions.C: mistakes the OTHER single force's work (friction's) for the net work, with the same underlying error as B
distractor_misconceptions.D: adds the magnitudes of two opposing forces' work instead of summing them with their signs

questions.tested_idea: only the NET work changes kinetic energy; a force can do large real work while the net — and therefore K — does not move
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 4 kg crate coasts at a constant 3 m/s while an 11.76 N pull exactly balances 11.76 N of kinetic friction over 6 m. What is the net work done, and how does the kinetic energy change?

questions.stem: A 4 kg cart launched backward at 3 m/s is pulled by a steady 12 N forward force on a frictionless floor. By the time it has turned around and sped back up to 4.8 m/s, moving forward, its kinetic energy is 46.1 J. What is the net work done on the cart over this whole trip?

distractor_misconceptions.B: the exact planted misconception: reports the FINAL kinetic energy itself as the net work, dropping the starting kinetic energy entirely
distractor_misconceptions.C: adds the final and starting kinetic energies instead of subtracting them
distractor_misconceptions.D: stops at the turn-around instant's net-work reading instead of continuing to the end of the described trip

questions.tested_idea: net work is the CHANGE in kinetic energy measured from the START, not the final kinetic energy alone — true even through a velocity reversal
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 2 kg cart launched backward at 2 m/s is pulled by a steady 6 N forward force on a frictionless floor. Its starting kinetic energy is 4.0 J. By the time it has turned around and reached 4 m/s forward, its kinetic energy is 16.0 J. Find the net work done over the whole trip.

questions.stem: A 5 kg cart moving at 2 m/s is accelerated by a steady 5 N pull on a frictionless floor. By the time it has moved 2 m, what is the net work done, and what is the cart's kinetic energy at that point?

distractor_misconceptions.B: computes the net work correctly but reports only the CHANGE as the new total, forgetting to add it to the starting kinetic energy
distractor_misconceptions.C: uses half the distance (1 m instead of 2 m) in computing the pull's work
distractor_misconceptions.D: overstates the final kinetic energy, effectively double-counting the added work

questions.tested_idea: the derivation W_net = ma*d = half m v squared minus half m v-naught squared, checked numerically against the starting kinetic energy
questions.parallel_form_stem: A 3 kg cart moving at 1 m/s is accelerated by a steady 6 N pull on a frictionless floor. After it has moved 3 m, find the net work done and the cart's kinetic energy.

questions.stem: In the sandbox, you set the pull below the force needed to overcome friction, so the crate stays at rest the whole time. Using the theorem W_net = delta K, what must the net work on the crate be, and why?

options.A: 0 J, because the kinetic energy never changes from zero
options.B: 0 J, because no force is acting on the crate
options.C: A large negative value, because friction is holding the crate back
options.D: It cannot be determined without knowing the exact forces

distractor_misconceptions.B: denies that any force acts at all — the pull and static friction both act, they simply sum to zero
distractor_misconceptions.C: mistakes ONE force's (friction's) work for the net work, the same error class as q3's headline misconception
distractor_misconceptions.D: misses the theorem's own power: the net work is determined directly from the change in kinetic energy, with no need to know the individual forces at all

questions.tested_idea: the theorem transfers to any configuration, including one at rest: zero change in kinetic energy means exactly zero net work, regardless of how many individual forces are acting
questions.parallel_form_stem: In a similar sandbox, a small pull never overcomes static friction and a crate stays at rest for the whole run. What is the net work done on the crate?
